title: Graduated Commit Discount Bridge & Contract Grace Window
creator: Aaliyah Park
description:
Problem: Mid-term expansions (seat or token growth) during multi-year contracts create negotiation friction, retrospective billing disputes, and lost revenue when customers expect full term discounts for incremental additions. Current true-up flows are manual, prone to delays, and cause churn risk during renewal.

Proposal: Introduce a graduated commit discount bridge and a 30-day contract grace window to simplify intra-term expansion. Key components: (1) Graduated bridge bands - when a customer expands capacity mid-term, new units fall into a time-weighted discount band (eg. months remaining determine pro-rated discount tier). (2) Contract grace window - allow customers a single 30-day window after an expansion to elect to convert the expansion into a formal commit with a blended multi-year discount applied prospectively. (3) Auto-true-up opt-in - for qualifying enterprise customers we enable optional auto-true-up where overages are automatically converted to the nearest committed tier at end-of-quarter unless customer opts out. (4) Clear contract language and SOW template updates to embed bridge and grace mechanics and ensure auditability for security questionnaire reviewers.

Why different: Unlike a simple true-up or blanket multi-year uplift, this approach balances customer flexibility with predictable economics for Redwood by: enabling short-term adoption without immediate long-term commitment, improving renewal retention through a simple conversion pathway, and reducing back-and-forth for AE/CS teams.

Metrics & success criteria: target +8% net revenue retention for accounts >$50k ARR that expand mid-term, reduce manual true-up tickets by 60% in Q2 pilot, maintain effective gross margin on expanded units within 5% of baseline.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Phase 0 (Legal / Finance): finalize contract wording & invoice mechanics, tax implications, and accounting treatment for revenue recognition. Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/REV/Commit+Bridge+Spec
- Phase 1 (Pilot): select 12 enterprise accounts across sales verticals; enable bridge bands and a manual grace-window process; collect telemetry on conversions and CS friction. Internal dashboard: https://dash.redwood.com/d/renewals/commit-bridge-pilot
- Phase 2 (Automation): productize billing proration and grace-window UI in Console; add auto-true-up configuration in account settings; backend work with billing/Gateway. GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pulls?q=commit-bridge
- Phase 3 (Rollout): update standard contract templates, SSO/SAML questionnaire guidance, and rep playbook; run enablement for AE/CS.

Trade-offs & risks: Pricing complexity may confuse smaller customers; administrative cost for managing grace-window exceptions; potential ARR timing shifts that require finance forecasting adjustments. Mitigations: limit feature to committed tiers >$25k ARR for initial rollout, provide clear UI copy and short explainer video, and partner with Finance for forecasting macros.
acceptance_criteria: Legal sign-off on contract language and SOW templates referencing bridge and grace window
Billing team validated proration calculations and invoice format for pilot accounts
Pilot completed with 12 accounts and dashboarded conversion metrics
Console has a basic UI toggle to opt into auto-true-up and displays remaining grace window for expansions
AE/CS playbook drafted and 2 enablement sessions recorded
